The CBOR payload is decoded by libcbor; the resulting cbor_item_t tree contains attacker-controlled maps, arrays, and integer values.

fine_trace.code: pairs = cbor_map_handle(item); for (gsize i = 0; i < cbor_map_size(item); i++) { FuCoswidTag tag_id = cbor_get_uint8(pairs[i].key); ... }

fine_trace.code: if (cbor_isa_uint(pairs[i].value)) { FuCoswidEntityRole role = cbor_get_uint8(pairs[i].value); entity->roles[entity_role_cnt++] = role; }
fine_trace.note: When the ROLE tag value is a CBOR unsigned integer, the code writes entity->roles[entity_role_cnt++] without checking that entity_role_cnt is below G_N_ELEMENTS(entity->roles) (6). If entity_role_cnt is already 6, this writes out of bounds.

Even when the value is a uint (not an array), the loop still calls cbor_array_size(pairs[i].value) on the non-array item, reading from the item's data union (8 bytes) which may be uninitialized or out of bounds for small integer items.
